# Create Samebase app (`create_repository`)

MCP tool `repository_actions_createRepository` · scope `access_app_create` · write

Creates a Samebase app in one action. It always creates a GitHub repository under the selected
organization's verified GitHub owner, seeds the starter template, and creates a Convex project with
one production deployment. It uses convexDeploymentRegion when supplied. Otherwise, it uses the
organization default, which is US East when no default is saved. When cloudflareBuildTokenUuid is a
current token UUID, it also creates a Cloudflare Worker and configures Workers Builds for the
repository (pushes to the default branch deploy, and pull requests get preview deploys) with Convex
deploy keys in the build triggers.

Pass null only after cloudflare_listWorkersBuildTokens returns an empty current list. In that case,
the run creates no Cloudflare Worker and stops after GitHub and Convex are ready. Cloudflare setup
is still pending. Follow https://samebase.com/docs/cloudflare-setup: use Cloudflare's standard
repository setup to create the first account token, delete the temporary Worker, then use
repository_cloudflare_createWorker with a current token UUID to create and configure the real
Worker.

Preconditions: the caller must be an organization member. Its GitHub App installation and selected
Convex and Cloudflare provider connections must be available. The GitHub repository and Convex
project names must be available. The Cloudflare Worker name must be available only when a token UUID
requests automatic Cloudflare provisioning. A required cloudflareWorkerName is ignored when the
token is null. A relevant name collision fails the call immediately before any repository or run is
created, so pick a different name and call again; failures after provisioning starts surface through
`repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories` instead.

What it writes: one repository (private by default) and one Convex project with one production
deployment in the resolved region. When `cloudflareBuildTokenUuid` is not null, it also writes one
Worker and two Workers Builds triggers that each carry a scoped `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` variable. The
production trigger receives the production deploy key and the readable `SAMEBASE_CONVEX_PROJECT`
marker. The preview trigger receives the project Preview deploy key. All resources live in the
organization's provider accounts. Deleting the Samebase account does not remove or stop any of them.

Progress and failure are readable through `repository_dashboard_getUserRepositories`: while running,
`providerSetup` carries the current step; on failure it carries the failed step and a message.
Repair it with `repository_actions_retryInfrastructureProvisioning`. When the token was null,
`providerSetup.status: ready` means that the requested GitHub and Convex work finished. It does not
mean Cloudflare is complete. This expected pending state is not a failure and must not be repaired
with the retry action. Cost: the created resources run on the providers' free tiers; an idle app
costs $0/month.

## Arguments

- `githubOwnerLogin` (string, required): GitHub owner login that will own the new repository.
- `githubRepositoryName` (string, required): Name for the new GitHub repository and Samebase app.
- `convexProjectName` (string, required): Convex project name to provision for the app.
- `convexDeploymentRegion` (value, optional): Optional production region override: aws-us-east-1,
  aws-eu-west-1, aws-ca-central-1, or aws-ap-southeast-2. Omit it to use the organization default,
  which is US East when no default is saved.
- `cloudflareWorkerName` (string, required): Cloudflare Worker name for automatic Cloudflare
  provisioning. This required field is ignored when cloudflareBuildTokenUuid is null.
- `cloudflareBuildTokenUuid` (value, required): Exact Workers Builds token UUID returned by
  cloudflare_listWorkersBuildTokens, or null only after that current list is confirmed empty.
- `description` (string, optional): Optional GitHub repository description.
- `private` (boolean, optional): Whether to create a private GitHub repository. Defaults to true.
